title: Advances in transition-metal-catalyzed C7-functionalization of indolines: pyrimidine-directed strategies
content: Transition-metal-catalyzed C–H functionalization has become a central strategy for the direct and selective elaboration of organic molecules through the activation of otherwise inert C–H bonds. Among the nitrogen-based directing groups developed for this purpose, the 2-pyrimidyl group has proven particularly effective for the challenging functionalization of the benzenoid ring of indolines at the C7 position. The indoline core is a recurring structural element of natural products, pharmaceuticals and functional materials, yet selective functionalization of its C7–H bond is complicated by the presence of several electronically and sterically similar C–H bonds. This review summarises recent progress in pyrimidine-directed, transition-metal-catalyzed C7–H functionalization of indolines. It covers C–C bond-forming transformations (alkylation, arylation, allylation, alkenylation, alkynylation, acylation and carbonylation) as well as C–N, C–O, C–S, C–Se and C–X bond formation and annulation reactions. Particular attention is paid to the influence of the metal catalyst, coupling partner, directing-group coordination and reaction conditions on substrate scope, functional-group tolerance and limitations, and to the mechanistic proposals that account for the observed selectivity. Taken together, these studies show that the pyrimidine-directed strategy is an efficient means of overriding the innate reactivity of indoline and achieving highly selective C7 functionalization.
